declarations.checkedType: agent(calendar_id: string, description?: string, end: string, recurrence?: array[string], start: string, summary: string, time_zone?: string) -> event with credential | throw[api_error | auth_error | fetch_error | parse_error] | io
declarations.documentation:
Tool: create an event on a calendar — one event, or a whole recurring series in a single call when
@recurrence@ is given. @calendar_id@ is the target calendar ("primary" for the user's own); @summary@ is
the title; @start@ / @end@ are RFC3339 timestamps (e.g. "2026-07-11T15:00:00+09:00") and, for a
recurring event, describe its first occurrence, which the rule then repeats; @description@ is optional
detail.

@recurrence@ holds RFC 5545 recurrence rules, passed to Google verbatim — Google validates them, and a
malformed rule comes back as an `http.api_error`. Almost always one "RRULE:..." string:

  - every Wednesday and Sunday, up to and including 2026-08-31:
    ["RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=WE,SU;UNTIL=20260831T000000Z"]
  - every weekday for the next 10 occurrences: ["RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR;COUNT=10"]
  - the same day of every month, with no end: ["RRULE:FREQ=MONTHLY"]

A series ends by `UNTIL` (a compact UTC timestamp — `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ`, no dashes or colons, unlike
@start@ / @end@ — and inclusive) or by `COUNT` (a number of occurrences); give one or neither, never both.
Omit both for a series that runs forever. Weekdays are the two-letter `MO TU WE TH FR SA SU`.

@time_zone@ is an IANA zone name ("Asia/Tokyo", "America/New_York") and is required whenever
@recurrence@ is given: Google expands the rule in that zone, which is what fixes whose 10:00 "every
Wednesday at 10:00" means and keeps an occurrence at 10:00 local across a daylight-saving shift. A
recurring event without it is rejected as an `http.api_error` (a 400). A single event needs none — an
RFC3339 offset already fixes one instant.

Returns the created event. For a recurring one that is the series master: its start / end are the first
occurrence's, and its id addresses the whole series (`update_event` on it changes every occurrence,
`delete_event` on it removes them all). List the window with `list_events` to see the individual
occurrences.
declarations.name: create_event

declarations.documentation:
Tool: update an existing event on a calendar. @calendar_id@ is the calendar ("primary" for the user's
own) and @event_id@ the event's id (from `list_events` / `create_event`). Only the fields you pass are
changed: @summary@ (title), @start@ / @end@ (RFC3339 timestamps, e.g. "2026-07-11T15:00:00Z") and
@description@ each default to `null`, which leaves the field exactly as it is, while passing `""` empties
it — that is how a @summary@ or @description@ is cleared. @start@ and @end@ have no empty form, so pass a
timestamp or leave them alone; an empty one is a 400 from Google. Returns the updated event.

The id you pass decides the reach on a recurring event: the series-master id (what `create_event` returned)
edits every occurrence at once, and one occurrence's id (what `list_events` returns) edits only that one,
recorded as an exception to the series. There is no third reach — "this and all following" is not
something this tool expresses. The recurrence rule itself is not patchable here — to change a series'
schedule or its end date, `delete_event` the master and `create_event` a new series.

declarations.documentation:
Tool: delete an event from a calendar. @calendar_id@ is the calendar ("primary" for the user's own)
and @event_id@ the event's id (from `list_events` / `create_event`); a deletion cannot be undone, and
deleting an already-gone event comes back as a plain `http.api_error` (a 404/410). On a recurring event
the id decides the reach as in `update_event`: the series-master id removes the whole series, one
occurrence's id cancels just that occurrence. Returns null.
declarations.name: delete_event

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for something other than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is
not 401 / 403. Which failures are worth repeating is read off @status@ — 408 / 429 / 5xx are the
transient ones, and every other status repeats its answer until the argument changes — which is why
the status rides on the error rather than being folded into a sentence. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body verbatim.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over the identity of the caller: the endpoint answered 401 or
403, so the credential is what failed — revoked, expired, or scoped too narrowly. Retrying with the
same credential gives the same answer; the recovery is a fresh resolution of it, so the ordinary
composition is a `supervise` converter signalling `supervise.interrupted`. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words and @message@ carries the server's own body, kept apart so a renderer
can show either alone.

403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion; a quota 403 that is
replayed answers the same way.

declarations.checkedType: agent(calendar_id: string, cursor_at: fresh | resume, deliver_to: agent(value: event) -> null with E2, lead_time_milliseconds: number, poll_interval_milliseconds: number) -> never with credential | throw[watch_misconfigured | api_error | auth_error | fetch_error | parse_error] | get | set | E2 | io
declarations.documentation:
Watch a calendar for upcoming timed events and deliver each one to @deliver_to@ as it enters the lead
window — `poll.subscribe` under a Calendar adapter, so it composes under `parallel [ … ]` and never
resolves (`-> never`). Every @poll_interval_milliseconds@ it lists the events whose start lies within
@lead_time_milliseconds@ ahead of the tick and delivers each one not seen before. It covers timed events;
an all-day event has no instant to place in the window. @deliver_to@'s effects @E@ flow to the caller's
handlers unchanged.

Delivery is at-least-once: the commit lands only after a delivery returns, so a crash or a throw in
between re-delivers exactly that event on the next tick. Build exactly-once at the destination by making
the delivery idempotent on the dedup key.

The dedup key is `id ++ " " ++ start` and the memory is the last 200 of them (`poll.seen_set`): what a
calendar offers is a transition into the window rather than a receive clock a cursor could follow. An
event whose start has not moved is delivered once; an event whose start moved is a different key and
re-notifies, which is the answer a rescheduled meeting wants. 200 is far above what one lead window holds;
a calendar that delivered 200 events while one was still inside its own window could re-notify that one.
Recurring events need nothing special — the listing expands them per occurrence.

The events already inside the lead window when the subscription starts are recorded rather than delivered:
what it reports is an event entering the window from then on, and `list_events` answers what is coming up.

@cursor_at@ decides what a restart does and has no default. `poll.resume(key = ...)` keeps the memory in
the store, so a restart comes back holding the keys it already delivered; `poll.fresh()` re-primes on the
activation's first poll instead. Neither backfills, since a seen-set subscription has no floor to list
from. Two watches sharing one key overwrite each other's memory.

@poll_interval_milliseconds@ must not exceed @lead_time_milliseconds@, since the gap (T+lead, T+poll)
belongs to no window; a wider interval is rejected at entry with `watch_misconfigured`.

No retry is built in — a poll failure propagates and kills the subscription — so compose resilience by
wrapping the watch in a supervise provider. The first poll is one @poll_interval_milliseconds@ in and is
the priming one, so the earliest notification comes two intervals after the start.

effects.rendered: E | io | credential | store.get | store.set | prelude.throw[watch_misconfigured | http.api_failure | http.fetch_error | json.parse_error]

declarations.documentation:
List every timed event whose start lies in the window [@window_start@, @window_start@ + @lead@), across
all result pages — `watch`'s per-poll listing, drained through `google_common.paged` so a busy window
arrives in full. Internal to `watch`.
